detail.body:
## Purpose

Fixes incorrect attention behavior for prefix-LM multimodal models (e.g., Gemma3) on ROCm. This is a correctness fix. 

**Root cause:** Both `RocmAttentionBackend` and `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend` overrode
`supports_mm_prefix()` to return `True`, but neither backend actually implements the
`mm_prefix_range_tensor` passing required for bidirectional image-token attention during prefill. As a result,
prefix-LM multimodal models on ROCm were silently falling through with wrong attention masks and
image tokens were not attending to each other bidirectionally as required by models like Gemma3.

**Changes:**
1. **`rocm_attn.py` / `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`**: Removed the incorrect
   `supports_mm_prefix() -> True` overrides. Both backends now inherit the base-class default
   (`False`), causing the attention backend selector to correctly defer to Triton unified
   attention for prefix-LM models on ROCm.
2. **`gemma3_mm.py`**: Explicitly sets `config.text_config.is_mm_prefix_lm = True` in the
   multimodal constructor, since the text-only Gemma3 path does not set this flag but the
   multimodal path requires it for correct image-token attention.
3. **`rocm.py`**: Ports the `disable_chunked_mm_input` guard from the CUDA platform path to
   ROCm. For prefix-LM multimodal models, chunked prefill can split a multimodal item and
   break the intended bidirectional attention pattern; this ensures ROCm disables it
   automatically, matching CUDA behavior.
4. **`tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py`**: Adds a regression test
   asserting that both ROCm backends do not claim `mm_prefix` support, guarding against this
   being re-introduced silently.

## Test Plan

**Unit test (ROCm):**
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_attention_selector.py \
  -v -k test_rocm_backends_do_not_support_mm_prefix
```

lm-eval benchmarks ran are as follows:

Text-only tasks (lmeval) - HellaSwag, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, BoolQ, WinoGrande (Gemma3 4B and 12B):
```bash
# 4B
python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=2048,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \
    --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \
    --batch_size 16

# 12B
python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=2048,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \
    --tasks hellaswag,arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,boolq,winogrande \
    --batch_size 16
```

Multimodal task - `MMMU-val`:
```bash
# 4B
python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm-vlm \
    --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,max_images=1,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \
    --tasks mmmu_val \
    --batch_size 4 \
    --apply_chat_template

# 12B
python -m lm_eval \
    --model vllm-vlm \
    --model_args "pretrained=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,max_images=1,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \
    --tasks mmmu_val \
    --batch_size 4 \
    --apply_chat_template
```


## Test Result
No regression observed here.  Hardware used was `AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700`

**Gemma3-4B**:

### Text benchmarks 
**Gemma3-4B**:

| Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta |
|------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:|

| arc_easy | 0.8249 ± 0.0078 | 0.8237 ± 0.0078 | -0.0012 |
| boolq | 0.8410 ± 0.0064 | 0.8407 ± 0.0064 | -0.0003 |
| hellaswag | 0.5583 ± 0.0050 | 0.5591 ± 0.0050 | +0.0008 |
| piqa | 0.7644 ± 0.0099 | 0.7639 ± 0.0099 | -0.0005 |
| winogrande | 0.6969 ± 0.0129 | 0.6938 ± 0.0130 | -0.0031 |

**Gemma3-12B**:

| Task | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta  |
|------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:|
| arc_challenge | 0.6092 ± 0.0143 | 0.6118 ± 0.0142 | +0.0026 |
| arc_easy | 0.8342 ± 0.0076 | 0.8350 ± 0.0076 | +0.0008 |
| boolq | 0.8746 ± 0.0058 | 0.8743 ± 0.0058 | -0.0003 |
| hellaswag | 0.6270 ± 0.0048 | 0.6271 ± 0.0048 | +0.0001 |
| piqa | 0.8036 ± 0.0093 | 0.8003 ± 0.0093 | -0.0033 |
| winogrande | 0.7451 ± 0.0122 | 0.7482 ± 0.0122 | +0.0031 |

### Multimodal benchmark (MMMU-val)

| Model | Baseline (before fix) | With fix | Delta  |
|-------|:---------------------:|:--------:|:---:|
| Gemma3-4B-IT | 0.4067 ± 0.0157 | 0.4133 ± 0.0158 | +0.0066 |
| Gemma3-12B-IT | 0.4856 ± 0.0159 | 0.4922 ± 0.0158 | +0.0066 |

### **Edit: 24 July 2026**

#### Reproducing the benchmarks

**Additional multimodal tasks (lmms-eval)** - DocVQA, InfoVQA, AI2D, ChartQA, VQAv2 (Gemma3 4B and 12B):

```bash
# 4B
python -m lmms_eval eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "model=google/gemma-3-4b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85" \
    --tasks ai2d,chartqa,docvqa_val,infovqa_val,vqav2_val \
    --batch_size 8 \
    --limit 1000 \
    --seed 0

# 12B
python -m lmms_eval eval \
    --model vllm \
    --model_args "model=google/gemma-3-12b-it,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.95" \
    --tasks ai2d,chartqa,docvqa_val,infovqa_val,vqav2_val \
    --batch_size 8 \
    --limit 1000 \
    --seed 0
```

> 
> Note: the `lmms-eval==0.7.2` wheel ships **without** the `_default_template_*_yaml` task templates, so install it editable from the tag:
> `git clone --branch v0.7.2 https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval && pip install -e ./lmms-eval --no-deps && pip install decord Levenshtein`
>

+def test_rocm_backends_do_not_support_mm_prefix():
+    """Regression test: ROCm backends must not claim mm_prefix support.
+
+    If they do, prefix-LM multimodal models that attend vision tokens
+    bidirectionally (e.g. Gemma3 4B) will use bidirectional attention
+    via the ROCm backend instead of falling back to Triton, producing
+    incorrect results. Remove this test only if support is properly added.
+    """
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.rocm_aiter_unified_attn import (
+        RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend,
+    )

+
+    assert not RocmAttentionBackend.supports_mm_prefix(), (
+        "RocmAttentionBackend does not support mm_prefix — "
+        "defer to Triton unified attention instead for now"
+        "See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48172"
+    )
+    assert not RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend.supports_mm_prefix(), (
+        "RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend does not support mm_prefix — "
+        "defer to Triton unified attention instead for now"
+        "See https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/4168"
+    )

inline_comments.body:
> We somehow need to track this. It's a missing feature, isnt it?

Yes, it is a missing feature and should be added at ROCm side. But the kernel on our side is also Triton (on ROCM_ATTN) so deferring to Triton_ATTN for now should be fine. 

Since there are not many prefix lm models, we should still track it so that we can add a kernel for the same later on. I am not sure who maintains the ROCm backend on vLLM so not sure who to reach out regarding this. I was also hoping that you guys will be able to give me more insight into this issue on ROCm side. @AndreasKaratzas

+def test_rocm_backends_do_not_support_mm_prefix():
+    """Regression test: ROCm backends must not claim mm_prefix support.
+
+    If they do, prefix-LM multimodal models that attend vision tokens
+    bidirectionally (e.g. Gemma3 4B) will use bidirectional attention
+    via the ROCm backend instead of falling back to Triton, producing
+    incorrect results. Remove this test only if support is properly added.
+    """

+        "RocmAttentionBackend must not support mm_prefix — "
+        "defer to Triton unified attention instead"
+    )

+        "RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionBackend must not support mm_prefix — "
+        "defer to Triton unified attention instead"
+    )
